newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: AMS 9-mth figures battered by subsidiaries.
newsitem.headline: AMS 9-mth figures battered by subsidiaries.

text.p: Chip-maker Austria Mikro Systeme International AG (AMS) reported on Thursday a nine-month group pre-tax profit of 58 million schillings on sales of 1.439 billion schillings.
In the parent company, AMS said sales fell 26.6 percent to 989.6 million schillings and pre-tax profit slumped 32.7 percent to 148 million schillings.
Comparative group figures are not available as AMS made two acquisitions -- South Africa's SAMES and Germany's Thesys -- in late 1995.
On September 30, group order backlog stood at 583.7 million schillings, while incoming orders for the first nine months reached 996.1 million schillings.
In the parent, the order backlog stood 52.1 percent lower at 346.7 million schillings, while incoming orders fell 40.5 percent to 789 million schillings.

AMS's 51.25 percent-owned subsidiary Thesys Gesellschaft fuer Mikroelektronik GmbH turned in a loss of 155.4 million schillings on sales of 339.5 million compared to a loss of 83.9 million posted in the the first six months of 1996.
Thesys reported sales of 270.1 million schillings in the first half.
AMS' 51-percent-owned South African Micro-Electronic Systems Ltd (SAMES) whipped up a loss of 77.6 million schillings on turnover of 123.4 million.
In the first half, SAMES' loss stood at 64.9 million and sales at 87.6 million schillings.
The parent company's nine-month pre-tax profit of 148 million schillings is just 20 million schillings above that posted for the first six months.

In a statement, AMS said the nine-month group pre-tax profit of 58 million schillings largely came from the 148 million of the parent company, 39.6 million loss from its share in SAMES and 79.6 million loss from its share in Thesys.

AMS attributed the weak earnings figures to an overall deterioration in the semiconductor market this year. SAMES' results were particularly battered by the cancellation of a silicon foundry contract by a major U.S. customer.
Moreover, AMS has been hit by shorter order intakes and shorter delivery times for new projects.
AMS said it expected to continue feeling the brunt of the downturn in the semiconductor market into the new year, but declined to give further details.
